title: Disaster Preparedness Quiz
description: Are you ready for an emergency? Take the 5-minute quiz and find out.

questions.question: Do you have at least 1 gallon of water per person per day for 3 days stored?
choices: Yes, I have 3+ days of water stored
I have 1-2 days of water stored
I have some water but not enough
No, I rely on tap water only
questions.explanation: FEMA recommends storing at least 1 gallon per person per day for at least 3 days. This covers drinking and sanitation needs.

products.name: WaterBrick Stackable Water Storage Container (3.5 Gallon, 4-Pack)

questions.question: Do you have a water filter or purification tablets for emergency use?
choices: Yes, I have a filter AND tablets
I have one or the other
No, I don't have any water purification method
questions.explanation: Having multiple water purification methods ensures you can make water safe to drink if your stored supply runs out.

products.name: Potable Aqua Water Purification Tablets (50 count)

questions.question: Do you know how to shut off your home's water main?
choices: Yes, but I've never actually done it
I know where it is but not how to shut it off
No, I don't know where it is
questions.explanation: Knowing how to shut off your water main can prevent flooding in case of broken pipes during a disaster.

questions.question: Do you have at least 3 days of non-perishable food stored?
choices: Yes, 3+ days for everyone in household
I have some canned goods but not organized
No, I shop frequently and keep minimal food
questions.explanation: FEMA recommends a minimum 3-day supply of non-perishable food that requires no refrigeration or cooking.

questions.question: Do you have a manual can opener?
choices: Yes, and I know where it is
Yes, but I'm not sure where it is
No, I only have an electric can opener
questions.explanation: Electric can openers won't work during a power outage. A manual can opener is essential for accessing canned emergency food.

products.name: OXO Good Grips Smooth Edge Can Opener

questions.question: Do you have special dietary needs covered (baby formula, pet food, medications)?
choices: Yes, all special needs covered for 3+ days
questions.explanation: Don't forget about infants, pets, and anyone with dietary restrictions or medical needs when planning emergency supplies.

questions.question: Do you have blankets or sleeping bags for each person in your household?
choices: We have some but not enough
questions.explanation: Emergency blankets or sleeping bags can keep you warm if heating fails or you need to evacuate.

products.name: Teton Sports Celsius XL Sleeping Bag

questions.question: Do you have tarps or emergency shelter materials?
questions.explanation: Tarps are versatile for creating temporary shelter, covering broken windows, or protecting belongings.

questions.question: Do you know how to turn off your home's gas and electricity?
choices: I know how but haven't practiced
I know where the controls are
questions.explanation: Knowing how to shut off utilities can prevent fires, explosions, and electrocution after a disaster.

questions.question: Do you have a battery-powered or hand-crank emergency radio?
choices: Yes, with extra batteries or hand-crank
No, I rely on my phone
questions.explanation: Cell networks often fail during disasters. An emergency radio ensures you can receive critical weather and emergency alerts.

products.name: Midland ER310 Emergency Crank Weather Radio
FosPower Emergency Solar Hand Crank Radio

questions.question: Do you have a written emergency contact list (not just stored in your phone)?
choices: Yes, printed and kept with emergency supplies
Yes, but only in my phone
questions.explanation: If your phone dies or is lost, a written contact list ensures you can still reach family, emergency services, and important contacts.

questions.question: Do you have a designated meeting place if your family gets separated?
choices: Yes, both local and out-of-area meeting places
questions.explanation: Having a predetermined meeting place helps reunite family members when communication systems are down.

questions.question: Do you have a well-stocked first aid kit?
choices: Yes, comprehensive kit with supplies for major/minor injuries
Yes, basic kit with bandages and antiseptic
questions.explanation: A comprehensive first aid kit can treat injuries when medical help is delayed or unavailable.

products.name: Lightning X Premium First Aid Kit (300+ pieces)

questions.question: Do you have at least 7 days of prescription medications stored?
choices: Yes, 7+ days for all needed medications
No extra medications stored / Not needed
questions.explanation: Pharmacies may be closed or inaccessible during disasters. A week's supply gives you time to find alternative sources.

questions.question: Do you know CPR or basic first aid?
choices: I was trained but need a refresher
I've watched videos but no formal training
questions.explanation: Basic first aid and CPR skills can save lives when professional medical help is delayed.

products.name: Red Cross First Aid Training Course

questions.question: Do you have flashlights with extra batteries or hand-crank lights?
choices: Yes, multiple lights with backup power sources
Yes, one or two flashlights with batteries
I rely on my phone flashlight
questions.explanation: Multiple light sources ensure you can navigate safely during power outages.

questions.question: Do you have a backup power source (generator, solar charger, or power bank)?
choices: I've thought about it but haven't purchased
questions.explanation: Backup power keeps critical devices charged and can run essential appliances during extended outages.

products.name: Goal Zero Nomad 10 Solar Panel with power bank

questions.question: Do you have copies of important documents in a waterproof container?
questions.explanation: Copies of insurance, ID, medical records, and financial documents speed recovery after disasters.

questions.question: Do you have adequate insurance coverage (home, renters, flood)?
choices: Yes, and I review it annually
Yes, but haven't reviewed in years
questions.explanation: Adequate insurance coverage is your financial safety net for rebuilding after a disaster.

leadGen.note: Get free insurance quotes - we may earn a commission

questions.question: Have you practiced your emergency plan with your household?
choices: We have a plan but haven't practiced
questions.explanation: Practicing your emergency plan ensures everyone knows what to do, reducing panic and confusion during actual emergencies.

ranges.label: ❌ Critical Risk
ranges.message: Your preparedness level is critically low. You're vulnerable to even minor disruptions. Start with the essentials: water, food, and a first aid kit.

ranges.label: ⚠️ High Risk
ranges.message: You have some basics, but significant gaps remain. Focus on covering all 5 categories: water, food, shelter, communications, and medical.

ranges.label: ✅ Moderate Preparedness
ranges.message: You're on the right track! Fill in the remaining gaps and practice your emergency plan to reach full readiness.

ranges.label: 🟢 Well Prepared
ranges.message: Excellent! You're well-prepared for most emergencies. Keep your supplies fresh and continue practicing your plan.

ranges.label: ⭐ Expert Level
ranges.message: Outstanding! You're an emergency preparedness expert. Consider helping neighbors and community members prepare.
